question: Describe the function of the small intestines
answer:
• Absorbs digested food molecules into the blood.
• Produces enzymes (amylase, protease, lipase) to complete digestion.
• Has villi to increase surface area for absorption.

question: Name the 7 food groups
answer: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Lipids (Fats), Vitamins, Minerals, Fibre, Water.

question: Name the 7 food groups and give their function
answer:
• Carbohydrates: Energy source.
• Proteins: Growth and repair.
• Lipids: Energy storage and insulation.
• Vitamins & Minerals: Health maintenance/prevent deficiency.
• Fibre: Keeps food moving through gut.
• Water: Chemical reactions and hydration.

question: Describe the test and positive result for the test for protein
answer:
• Add Biuret reagent to the food sample.
• Positive result: Changes from blue to purple/lilac.

question: Describe the test for simple sugars
answer:
• Add Benedict's solution to food sample and heat in a water bath (>80°C).
• Positive result: Changes from blue to green/yellow/brick-red (depending on concentration).

question: Name the food groups that someone going to need after a day of fasting and explain why
answer:
• Carbohydrates: Quick restoration of glucose for energy/respiration.
• Water: Rehydration for metabolic processes.
• Protein: Repair tissues and muscle maintenance.

question: Give an example of each food group
answer:
• Carbohydrate: Bread/Pasta.
• Protein: Chicken/Beans.
• Lipid: Butter/Olive oil.
• Vitamin: Citrus fruits (Vit C).
• Mineral: Milk (Calcium).
• Fibre: Wholemeal bread/Vegetables.
• Water: Water/Cucumber.

question: Explain what can cause inaccuracy of results when burning foods to determine energy content
answer:
• Heat lost to the surroundings/air instead of heating the water.
• Incomplete combustion/burning of the food item.
• Heat lost to the boiling tube/beaker.

question: Describe the method and positive result for testing food for starch
answer:
• Add a few drops of Iodine solution directly to the food sample.
• Positive result: Changes from orange-brown to blue-black.

question: Describe the method and positive result for testing food for lipid
answer:
• Mix sample with ethanol, shake, then pour into water (Sudan III alternative).
• Positive result: A cloudy white emulsion forms (or red layer with Sudan III).

question: Define an enzyme
answer: A biological catalyst that speeds up chemical reactions without being used up.

question: Name the enzymes that digest protein, starch and lipid
answer:
• Starch: Carbohydrase / Amylase.
• Protein: Protease.
• Lipid: Lipase.

question: Name products of the digestion of starch, protein and lipid
answer:
• Starch: Glucose / simple sugars.
• Protein: Amino acids.
• Lipid: Fatty acids and glycerol.

question: Describe the graph showing the effect of temperature on enzyme activity
answer:
• Activity increases up to the optimum temperature as kinetic energy increases.
• Beyond optimum, activity drops rapidly to zero because the active site denatures.

question: Describe the graph showing the effect of pH on enzyme activity
answer:
• Activity peaks at the optimum pH.
• Moving above or below the optimum causes activity to drop to zero as the enzyme denatures.

question: Define a drug
answer: A chemical substance that alters the way the body or mind functions.

question: Name four categories of illegal drugs
answer: Stimulants, Depressants, Hallucinogens, Painkillers / Opiates.

question: Compare the short and long-term effects of alcohol on the body
answer:
Short-term: Slowed reaction times, impaired judgment, slurred speech.

Long-term: Liver cirrhosis, brain damage, increased risk of heart disease.

question: Describe the effects of carbon monoxide on the body
answer:
• Binds irreversibly to haemoglobin in red blood cells.
• Reduces the blood's capacity to carry oxygen.

question: Describe the effect of tar on the body
answer:
• Damages cilia in the trachea/bronchi leading to mucus buildup.
• Contains carcinogens that cause lung cancer.

question: Describe the short-term effects of alcohol on the body
answer:
• Slows down brain activity / reaction times.
• Loss of balance and coordination.

question: Describe the long-term effects of alcohol on the body
answer:
• Liver damage (cirrhosis).
• Brain damage / addiction.
• Increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

question: Define diffusion.
answer: Net movement of particles from high to low concentration.

question: Describe how glucose enters the cell through diffusion.
answer: Moves down its concentration gradient across the cell membrane from high concentration outside to lower concentration inside the cytoplasm.

question: Define osmosis.
answer: Net movement of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution across a partially permeable membrane.

question: Describe what will happen to a carrot if placed in a highly concentrated sugar solution.
answer: Water leaves the carrot cells by osmosis, causing the tissue to shrink, lose mass, and become flaccid/soft.

question: Describe what will happen to a carrot if placed in a very dilute sugar solution.
answer: Water enters the carrot cells by osmosis, causing the tissue to gain mass, expand, and become turgid/firm.

question: Explain what will happen to a red blood cell after being soaked in different solutions.
answer: In dilute/hypotonic solution, it absorbs water and bursts (lysis); in concentrated/hypertonic solution, it loses water and shrinks (crenation).

question: Explain what will happen to a plant cell after being soaked in different solutions.
answer: In hypotonic solution, water enters making it turgid (cell wall prevents bursting); in hypertonic solution, water leaves causing plasmolysis.
